question: At what lifecycle point do Java instance variables receive their default initial values?

options.text: Only when explicit assignment statements are omitted by the compiler.
During class loading by the JVM before any instances are created.
Only when the constructor method finishes executing and returns the reference.
During memory allocation of the object on the heap, prior to constructor execution.

explanation: When an object is created with new, memory is allocated on the heap and all instance variables are automatically set to their default values (0, false, null) before constructors run.

question: What is the default initial value of elements in a newly instantiated Object array `new Object[5]`?

options.text: 0 converted to reference pointers.
A new empty Object instance for each slot.
null for every element in the array.
Undefined garbage pointers to random memory.

explanation: When an array of references is allocated, each element is initialized to the default reference value, which is null.

question: What is the default value of a static primitive boolean field declared in a class?

options.text: true, because static boolean flags default to an enabled state.
Undefined until the static initializer block executes.
false, matching the default initialization of instance boolean fields.
null, because static variables are boxed into wrapper objects.

explanation: Static fields (class variables) follow the exact same default value rules as instance variables: boolean fields default to false.

question: What is the default value for an uninitialized byte field in a Java object?

options.text: Undefined random byte value
(byte) 0
null
(byte) -1

explanation: All primitive integer types, including byte, receive a default value of zero: (byte) 0.

question: Why does Java require local variables to be explicitly initialized before use, unlike fields?

options.text: Because local variables are automatically zeroed by the JVM at runtime.
To prevent accidental logic bugs arising from uninitialized stack variables.
Because local variables default to null regardless of type.
Because stack memory cannot hold default values in JVM architecture.

explanation: Java enforces definite assignment for local variables to catch programming mistakes early at compile time. Heap fields receive default values for safety.
